one_liner: MU: RS 99 (best in watchlist), earnings Sep 30 — high-conviction catalyst setup but stock down 5% in chip sell-off; wait for stabilisation before entry.

price_action.intraday_story: MU is down ~5% from its recent close of $1,027 — part of a broad semiconductor sector sell-off. Today's -0.12% close after the larger recent decline suggests the acute selling pressure is easing. Volume slightly elevated, consistent with institutional repositioning rather than panic. Stock is pulling back into a potential support zone.

news_catalyst.headline: Micron earnings Sep 30 — analysts predict skyrocketing on memory supply shortage; stock down 5% in chip sell-off
news_catalyst.summary: MU is the highest-RS stock in the watchlist at 99 — it has skyrocketed 256% in 2026 on AI-driven memory demand. Q3 revenue was $41.5B driven by HBM (high-bandwidth memory) for AI chips. The company has signed multi-year supply contracts at floor prices — locking in revenue visibility. Earnings on Sep 30 are the key catalyst: analysts expect strong guidance given persistent memory supply shortage. The current 5% sell-off in the chip sector is the entry opportunity bears and bulls are watching. Motley Fool predicts the stock will skyrocket after the Sep 30 print.

technical.summary:
MU is in a strong uptrend with RS 99 — the highest in the watchlist. The 256% YTD run is extraordinary. EMA structure is strongly bullish (price > EMA-50 > EMA-200 by a wide margin). The current 5% pullback from $1,027 to $976 is small relative to the prior advance and could be a buyable dip ahead of the Sep 30 earnings.

Key support at $940 (prior consolidation). If MU holds above $940 with volume drying up over the next few sessions, a VCP-like tight base could form ahead of earnings. The risk is that earnings are already priced in after a 256% run — any miss or weak guidance would cause an outsized negative reaction. Setup score is 0 because no VCP/Wyckoff pattern is formally detected yet.

wyckoff_narrative: MU's extraordinary 256% YTD advance places it firmly in the Markup phase of Wyckoff. No reversal signals detected. The current 5% pullback is normal profit-taking within a strong trend. The test is whether supply is absorbed at $940-$980. If volume dries up on this pullback (drying up = vol ratio < 0.7x average for 3+ sessions), it would be a Last Point of Support setup ahead of the Sep 30 earnings catalyst. Watch for that pattern.

valuation.summary: MU's DCF shows ~13% upside to $1,100 using a 60% growth rate (reflecting the memory supply shortage driven pricing power) and 12% discount rate. The bull case at $1,500 assumes the AI memory cycle persists for 3+ years and floor-price contracts hold. The bear case at $650 reflects a memory cycle downturn. Signed long-term supply contracts are a material derisking factor for the bear case.

key_strengths: Multi-year supply contracts at floor prices
Q3 revenue $41.5B — AI memory demand exceptional
key_concerns: Earnings Sep 30 — high expectations, any miss is a large downside risk
Stock down 5% in recent chip sell-off — momentum pause
fundamentals.summary: MU is fundamentally compelling: memory supply shortage, locked-in contracts, AI tailwind. B grade reflects that valuation has run ahead of fundamentals after a 256% move. Upcoming earnings are the make-or-break moment — strong guidance would drive further upside; any miss at these multiples would be painful.

risks: Earnings Sep 30 — expectations very high after 256% run; miss or weak guide = large gap down
Chip sector sell-off continues below $940 support
Memory cycle reversal — supply shortage eases faster than expected
financials_summary: Most recent quarter revenue: $41.46B (up 73.7% QoQ) Gross margin 84.6%, net margin 68.1% — healthy spread Free cash flow $17.56B. FCF positive — earnings backed by real cash. Net cash position $18.6B (cash > debt) — strong balance sheet.
